name: Sparkwash
manufacturer: the Gray Zone technicians and back-alley rippers, most notably a collective in the Milwaukee corridor called 'the Shed'
description: A cocktail of dissolved chrome-interface lubricant (stripped from scrapped cyberware housings), synthetic norepinephrine analogue, and a proprietary mix of mineral salts that supposedly improves neural-to-chrome signal conductivity. Injected near augment junction points, it promises to overclock basic cyberware — and sometimes delivers. Just as often, it causes the chrome to run hot and seize.
effects: temporary 20-40% overclock of basic motor and sensory augments
mild stimulant effect from norepinephrine component
chrome limbs feel 'smoother' and more responsive for duration
side_effects: augment seizure — limbs or sensory chrome locking up mid-movement
chrome overheating causing tissue burns at mount points
permanent augment degradation with repeated use
in rare cases, cascading chrome failure across multiple systems
cultural_context: Sparkwash is popular with the Gray Zone laborers who have basic industrial chrome — loading arms, reinforced joints — and need to push performance on a job without being able to afford legitimate augment maintenance or upgrades. It's also used in underground combat sports where augmented fighters want an edge. Rippers who sell it are usually the same people who can (sometimes) fix the damage it causes, which is good for business.
story_hooks: A dock worker's loading arm seized mid-operation and crushed a coworker — now there's a question of liability, and the Sparkwash supply chain leads somewhere unexpected
Someone is selling Sparkwash cut with an industrial solvent that's eating augment housings from the inside out — the damage doesn't show for weeks
An underground fight promoter wants a player character to use Sparkwash for a high-stakes bout; the ripper who supplies it says this batch is different — better — and won't explain why
